headline.purpose: Page and section H1/H2, the CTA heading.

title.purpose: Project card titles, service rows, About rows (weight 600).

lead.purpose: Intros under headings, hero tagline, Approach statements.

body.purpose: Running text, card descriptions (max 60ch), nav links.

caption.purpose: The data voice: context tags, Role/Stack, hostnames, chips, screenshot captions, form labels. Uppercase mono.

shadows.name: overlap
shadows.purpose: Only on the phone capture where it physically overlaps a desktop screenshot. Never used for elevation.

motion.name: wall-drift
motion.value: translateY(-50%) 70s linear infinite (up) / 80s reverse (down); translateX(-50%) 60s below 1024px
motion.purpose: The wall of work, the one signature motion. Paused on hover, off-screen, or via the pause button; static under reduced motion.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll-reveal; gated behind html.js and prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: underline-draw
motion.purpose: Project title underline on card hover or focus.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Button 2px lift, arrow nudge, border/text shifts to gilt.

motion.name: frame-zoom
motion.purpose: Screenshot zoom inside its frame on project card hover.

components.name: Wall of Work
components.description: The hero's signature motion: two columns of real screenshots drifting in opposite directions under a masked fade; pausable, paused off-screen and on hover, static under reduced motion.
components.css: .ds-wall-wrap { position: relative; max-width: 30rem; padding-bottom: 2rem; } .ds-wall { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 1rem; height: 24rem; overflow: hidden; -webkit-mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent, #000 14%, #000 86%, transparent); mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent, #000 14%, #000 86%, transparent); } .ds-wall-col { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; } .ds-wall-col--down { margin-top: -6rem; } .ds-shot { margin: 0; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid var(--color-line, #32343b); border-radius: 5px; background: var(--color-surface, #202226); } .ds-shot div { aspect-ratio: 16 / 10; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #2b2e33 0 14%, var(--color-surface, #202226) 14%); } .ds-shot figcaption { padding: 0.55rem 0.75rem; border-top: 1px solid var(--color-line, #32343b); font-family: 'DM Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-muted, #9d9b91); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-wall-toggle { position: absolute; right: 0; bottom: 0; padding: 0.25rem 0; background: none; border: 0; cursor: pointer; font-family: 'DM Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-muted, #9d9b91); } .ds-wall-toggle:hover { color: var(--color-gilt, #c6a15b); } .ds-wall-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #dd4753); outline-offset: 2px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-wall-col { animation: ds-wall-up 40s linear infinite; } .ds-wall-col--down { animation: ds-wall-down 46s linear infinite; } .ds-wall-wrap:hover .ds-wall-col { animation-play-state: paused; } } @keyframes ds-wall-up { to { transform: translateY(-50%); } } @keyframes ds-wall-down { from { transform: translateY(-50%); } to { transform: translateY(0); } }

narrative.overview:
A dark, precise working surface where the shipped work is the hero. The world is committed dark (color-scheme: dark): a graphite ground, warm off-white ink, gilt for labels and the one primary action, and a single ruby mark as the only bold colour. The interface steps back so real screenshots of live client sites carry the page: they drift in the hero's wall of work, and they sit in hairline frames on every project card. Nothing on the surface is illustration; the imagery is the evidence.

The register is calm, exact, and workmanlike. Headings are Schibsted Grotesk, tight and confident at 600–700; every piece of data (roles, stacks, context tags, hostnames, form labels, button labels) speaks in uppercase DM Mono. Depth is tonal: one step from ground to surface, drawn with 1px hairlines. The single exception is physical overlap: a phone capture laid over the lower-right corner of a desktop screenshot casts one soft shadow, because it really sits on top.

Density is generous and editorial: a centered 72rem column, wide vertical rhythm, sections divided by full-width hairlines, lists divided by hairlines instead of boxed into cards. The world refuses the dark-mode-neon-startup look (no glows, no saturated gradients, no candy accents) and the generic Swiss-Helvetica grid it replaced.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite dark world, committed (`color-scheme: dark`), warm off-white ink.
Real screenshots of shipped sites are the imagery; no placeholders, no illustration.
One ruby accent, used as a single mark: never a fill, never a wall.
Gilt for mono labels, the one primary action, and the selected/hover state.
Two voices: Schibsted Grotesk (display/body) + DM Mono (all data/labels).
Depth by tonal step + hairlines; one soft shadow, only for the overlapping phone capture.
Sharp-by-default corners (2/5/10px); one signature motion (the wall), fully opt-out.

rules.name: The Single Mark Rule
rules.body: Ruby appears only as a mark: a dot, a short rule, a link, a focus ring. It never fills a surface. The closing CTA is a graphite panel with a gilt button, not a ruby band; if ruby covers an area larger than a dot or a line, the rule is broken.

rules.name: The Gilt Job Rule
rules.body: Gilt has three jobs: mono labels, the single primary action, and interactive state (hover/selected borders, hostname links). It is never body text, never a heading, never a large fill.

rules.name: The Context Mark Rule
rules.body: How a project came about is told with a tiny geometric mark, never a colour wash: Freelance is a ruby dot plus the word; macmac and Marvelous Digital appear as their own monochrome wordmarks. All three are 0.4rem and travel together wherever context appears (project cards, /work filter chips, the About page).

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Prose and headings are Schibsted Grotesk; anything that reads as data (labels, roles, stacks, tags, hostnames, buttons) is DM Mono, uppercase, tracked. A voice never crosses into the other's job.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings stand alone. No mono kicker or label sits above a section heading; mono labels only name data next to it (a `dt` beside its `dd`, a context tag above a card title that it describes).

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by a 1px `line` border and one tonal step, never by a shadow. The only shadow marks a literal physical overlap of one capture over another.

dos: Do let real screenshots of shipped sites be the imagery; crop them to 16:10 (desktop) or 390:844 (phone), top-anchored, inside a hairline frame.
Do keep ruby as a single mark: dots, a short rule, links, focus rings.
Do use gilt for mono labels, the one primary action, and hover/selected state.
Do mark project context with the dot / diamond / ring trio wherever context appears.
Do separate surfaces with the `line` hairline and one tonal step; divide lists with hairlines instead of boxing them into cards.
Do put all data (roles, stacks, tags, hostnames, labels, buttons) in DM Mono, uppercase, tracked.
Do draw icons as inline SVG strokes (1.5px, square caps) sized in `em`.
Do gate every animation behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, give continuous motion a pause control, and stop it when off-screen.
Do ship every visitor-facing string in both EN and FR (binding product constraint).
donts: Don't fill a surface with ruby or build a ruby band; the closing CTA is a graphite panel with a gilt button.
Don't add drop shadows for elevation; the only shadow is the phone capture's physical overlap.
Don't use placeholder imagery, stock illustration, or a portrait in place of real work.
Don't put a mono eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
Don't use unicode glyph arrows (→ ↗) or emoji as icons.
Don't introduce neon glows, saturated gradients, or a second bold accent.
Don't set body or heading text in gilt, or run prose in the mono voice.
Don't add a second continuous animation; the wall of work is the one signature motion.
Don't add a second display typeface or a system font; the pairing is fixed.
